method: Manual inspection of the six highest displayed-view Reels in an 80-tile profile-grid sample, plus one chakra progression case. Reactions/comments/shares are rounded visible counters from each active Reel; duration comes from its visible video element. No audio spectral measurement or private analytics access.

cases.title: Third-eye / purple bubbles
cases.visual: Large purple sphere with moving, lit bubbles; bold white/purple central type on a nearly black background.
cases.content: A provocative third-eye premise is paired with an advertised 963 Hz track, then an offer to send a free resource through DMs.
cases.hypothesis: The unusual organic surface and high-contrast hook interrupt scrolling. A single keyword plus a specific resource reduces the work needed to respond. The biological claims in this post are not substantiated by this analysis.

cases.title: Money magnet / pink orb
cases.visual: One illuminated pink sphere, thin orbit rings, restrained grid, a large identity-based affirmation above it.
cases.content: Abundance is framed as an identity and a morning ritual; the caption offers a link in response to a matching comment keyword.
cases.hypothesis: An immediately understood aspiration and one calm focal point make this easy to recognize without sound. This has the most visible reactions among the seven inspected cases, not necessarily across the entire page. Financial outcomes are not demonstrated.

cases.title: Wealth affirmation / orange orb
cases.visual: Warm orange breathing sphere, orbit arcs, light grid and a short affirmation; a small spectrum-like accent below.
cases.content: A first-person abundance affirmation leads into a multi-frequency explanation and an offer linking to a seven-day wealth resource.
cases.hypothesis: This is the clearest combination of aspiration, legible hook and concrete follow-up offer in the inspected group. It has the most visible comments among these seven. We cannot attribute those comments to the visual or CTA alone.

cases.title: Money-block release / frequency ladder
cases.visual: Stacked colored nodes, horizontal wave lanes and a moving rainbow loop, with a short topic heading.
cases.content: A financial-friction hook is reframed as a frequency issue, followed by a short practice and a free-resource prompt.
cases.hypothesis: The ladder suggests a multi-step system and gives the eye a path to follow. Pain-point recognition may help, but calling financial difficulties a frequency problem is a claim to avoid copying.

cases.title: Tone sweep / tilted resonance torus
cases.visual: A slowly turning, illuminated elliptical ring/torus; dark negative space and changing frequency labels.
cases.content: The post describes a root-to-crown sweep and asks the viewer to wait for a combined ending, then offers a free three-day resource.
cases.hypothesis: A promised ending gives a reason to keep watching, while smooth rotation makes repetition comfortable. It has the most shares among these seven, which suggests a useful sharing prompt to test—not proof of why it spread.

cases.title: Spiritual connection / luminous orb
cases.visual: A bright cyan-white core with moving filament rays, a dark field and a large question-led headline.
cases.content: The caption discusses the spiritual association of 963 Hz, explicitly notes that literal divine connection is unproven, and asks for viewers’ beliefs.
cases.hypothesis: A discussion question can work without a keyword giveaway. This is a useful counterexample to the idea that every successful post needs comment-to-DM bait.

cases.title: Seven-chakra progressive reveal
cases.visual: Seven vertically aligned chakra lights illuminate progressively; a visible request to watch the complete sequence.
cases.content: A root-to-crown progression offers a small completion goal and a collective ending. The on-video footer uses an alignment keyword; the expanded caption was not reviewed.
cases.hypothesis: Visible progression can give viewers a reason to stay. ZenWave already has a timed chakra build, so the immediate opportunity is clearer framing and CTA placement rather than replacing that feature.
